items.title: Persistent reasoning loop and memory spine
items.summary: The always-on daemon, three-tier memory, and local Gemma runtime are live and continuously growing.
items.details: Maez runs as a service, thinks every 30 seconds, stores observations, and never resets to zero.

items.title: Public web surface redesign
items.summary: Landing, login, app, progress, and dashboard now share a clearer, more human public experience built around continuity instead of generic AI-tool language.
items.details: The public site now leads with presence, continuity, and user understanding first, while keeping the existing auth flows, analytics hooks, and live status behavior intact.

items.title: Dashboard and progress proof layers
items.summary: The dashboard now reads as the technical proof layer, while progress explains how much of the idea has already become real.
items.details: This keeps the architecture map separate from the build-status story so first-time visitors can understand the concept before they go technical.

items.title: Whole-funnel UX clarification
items.summary: The public funnel now explains Maez in one consistent order: what it is, how it begins, how it keeps living, and why that matters.
items.details: Landing, login, app, progress, and dashboard now reuse the same thesis and proof ideas instead of reframing Maez differently on each page.

items.title: Live observation window
items.summary: Self-improvement is being observed carefully so Maez learns from live behavior before more autonomy is granted.
items.details: One proposal at a time. Slow observation over synthetic confidence.

items.title: Fast-lane traffic validation
items.summary: The fast reply lane exists in staging and still needs real-world validation before broader rollout.
items.details: The routing, redaction, audit, and policy layers are built; traffic confidence is what remains.

items.title: Public progress board and private planner
items.summary: Public progress and private planning now run as separate surfaces over one shared board model, with hidden notes staying private by default.
items.details: Public visitors read `/progress`; authenticated editing stays in `/planner`; the same data model feeds both views without exposing private scratch work.
items.private_notes: Keep private scratch ideas out of the public board by default.

items.title: Ship VAGUENESS_DETECTION routing fix
items.summary: Separate vague failures from repetition/fixation so self-diagnosis can route to the right corrective action.
items.details: This is the next high-leverage system fix from the observation window.

items.title: the owner desktop wrapper
items.summary: A closer daily wrapper around Maez is next once the current web and fast-lane surfaces settle.
items.details: This will likely become the most natural high-trust surface.

items.title: Publishing agent
items.summary: A supervised publishing flow for public updates is planned after the current communication surfaces stabilize.
items.details: This comes after the planner, desktop, and fast-lane validation work is mature.

items.title: Voice pipeline revival
items.summary: Voice returns later, once the infrastructure path is stable enough to justify reviving it properly.
items.details: Useful, but not ahead of the current system and UX priorities.

items.title: Elder deployment notes
items.summary: Private scratch area for mission-aligned deployment ideas.
items.private_notes: Think through onboarding, trust, pacing, screen simplicity, and non-technical caregiver roles.
